raw_review_excerpt:
Round-2 review of the Graphify hyperedge ID normalization patch plan. The plan's technical premise checks out against the current graphify source: export.py's attach_hyperedges() still does unsafe h["id"] lookups on already-stored hyperedge metadata (export.py:467), which is exactly the KeyError the plan targets, and build_merge()'s carry-forward path (build.py:1049-1063) reaches that function. The three prior-round concerns (cluster-only flags, upstream posture, synthesis/drop wording) are now resolved or non-blocking: --no-label/--no-viz flags on cluster-only are confirmed in __main__.py's help text, synthesis-vs-drop wording is now consistent across Success State/Architecture Decisions/Task 2/Risks, and the upstream-posture claim is unverifiable but is framed as non-blocking context rather than a load-bearing execution assumption. Referenced test files and reinstall extras are all real. The plan is execution-ready with only minor non-blocking tightening opportunities.

Issues:
- 1. [NOTE] Upstream-posture claim is unverifiable from local sources
- 2. [NOTE] Incident-artifact counts are asserted but not independently reverified this round
closure_verification: All three prior-round carried issues were checked against the current plan text and the current graphify source (not the caller's narrative alone). rubric_cards.title: attach_hyperedges() unsafe id access matches plan's root-cause claim
rubric_cards.claim: Plan Architecture Decision #2 claims attach_hyperedges() unsafely uses h["id"] on untrusted existing graph metadata and must be made defensive.
rubric_cards.evidence: Read graphify/export.py lines 464-472: `seen_ids = {h["id"] for h in existing}` operates on `existing = G.graph.get("hyperedges", [])` with no .get()/isinstance guard, exactly the KeyError('id') class described. build.py:1049-1063 shows build_merge() reaches this via the carried-hyperedges path when existing_hyperedges is non-empty.

rubric_cards.title: cluster-only recovery flags exist as claimed
rubric_cards.claim: Task 5 assumes `graphify cluster-only . --no-label --no-viz` is a valid non-LLM recovery command.
rubric_cards.evidence: CLI help text confirms `cluster-only <path>` supports `--no-viz` (skip HTML), `--no-label` (skip LLM community naming), and `--graph`/`--backend`/`--model` — matches the plan's Task 5 verify command and grep check.

rubric_cards.title: Synthesis-vs-drop wording is now internally consistent
rubric_cards.anchor: plan Success State / Architecture Decisions / Task 2 / Risks
rubric_cards.claim: Prior round flagged ambiguous synthesis/drop wording as an issue to resolve.
rubric_cards.evidence: Success State, Architecture Decision #1, Task 2 acceptance criteria, and the Risks section now uniformly describe: synthesize a deterministic ID for hyperedges with >=2 valid member nodes, drop only non-dict or unmeaningful entries. graphify/ids.py's make_id()/normalize_id() gives a ready-made deterministic-ID primitive matching the described approach (source_file, relation, label, member IDs).

Did not verify the external safishamsi/graphify upstream repo state (no URL access in scope for this review).

workflow_compliance: Plan includes explicit Task List with acceptance criteria, likely files touched, verify commands, and dependencies per task — matches expected plan structure.
Checkpoints (A/B/C) map cleanly onto task groupings and give clear go/no-go gates before code edits, before targeted-test completion, and before CLI reinstall.
Non-Goals section explicitly excludes scope creep (schema redesign, prompt changes, site-packages patching, broad multi-repo refresh, blocking the Pi rollout) — good anti-churn discipline.
Responsibility Boundaries section correctly maps to the actual module structure (build.py/export.py/cache.py) verified in this review.
technical_reality: graphify/export.py:464-472 attach_hyperedges() currently performs `h["id"]` on `existing` (already-stored) hyperedges with no defensive .get()/type check — this is the exact KeyError('id') failure mode the plan targets.

graphify/build.py's build_merge() (lines 1049-1063) calls attach_hyperedges(G, carried) whenever existing_hyperedges from a loaded graph.json is non-empty, which is the reachable crash path from an --update/incremental workflow.

graphify/build.py's build_from_json() stores hyperedges into G.graph['hyperedges'] essentially verbatim (line 786, only source_file relativization applied) — no id validation happens there, so malformed entries persist into G.graph until attach_hyperedges is invoked, consistent with the plan's Responsibility Boundaries characterization.
cluster-only's --no-label and --no-viz flags exist in the current CLI (confirmed in __main__.py help text) exactly as used in Task 5's verify commands.

graphify/ids.py provides make_id()/normalize_id(), a ready deterministic-ID primitive matching Architecture Decision #1's proposed synthesis approach (source_file, relation, label, normalized member IDs).

Task 4's `uv tool install --with openai --with tiktoken --with faster-whisper --with yt-dlp --with watchdog --with tree-sitter-sql` extras all correspond to real optional-dependency groups declared in pyproject.toml (kimi/openai, video, watch, sql).

All three test files named as 'Likely files touched' (test_hypergraph.py, test_build_merge_hyperedges_and_prune.py, test_extract_cli.py) exist and already contain related hyperedge/cli test scaffolding, reducing execution risk for Task 1.
assumptions_to_verify: Whether the real incident artifact still reproduces the specific counts cited (41/23 hyperedges, 15/5 cache entries) at the time Task 5 is actually executed — Task 5's own verify commands will surface this.
Whether upstream safishamsi/graphify v8 genuinely still has the same unsafe attach_hyperedges() implementation — stated as rationale only, not load-bearing for the fix itself.
verification_sufficiency: Sufficient: the plan's core technical premise (attach_hyperedges unsafe id access, build_merge's crash path, cluster-only flag availability, existence of named test files, validity of reinstall extras) was directly verified against the current repo source rather than taken on the caller's word.
Not independently re-verified: the exact incident-artifact counts and the upstream-repo claim, both external to this repo and non-blocking for freeze readiness.
downstream_risks: If Task 2's normalization helper is not actually shared between build.py and export.py (per Architecture Decision #3), attach_hyperedges() could remain unsafe for any caller other than build_merge's carried-hyperedge path (e.g. watch.py or a direct API caller) — worth confirming at implementation/review time that the helper is applied at both ingestion points, not just the one reproduced in Task 1's tests.

The safety-shrink check in build_merge (lines 1105-1114) is skipped when dedup or prune_sources is active; if Task 2's normalization drops any 'unusable' hyperedges silently, node/edge counts are unaffected so this guard won't catch a hyperedge-count regression — acceptable per plan's stated Non-Goals but worth a stderr log per the plan's Open Questions.
review.freeze_recommendation: Safe to freeze. Carry the remaining WARN/NOTE items as explicit follow-ups or implementation-time checks.
